title: Runtime surface contracts and failure isolation manual
author: Aisha Kumar
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document defines the runtime surface contracts between key inference stack components and prescribes failure-isolation boundaries, kernel-scheduling invariants, profiling hooks, and operational runbooks. The goal is to reduce cross-component blast radius, make failure modes attributable, and provide an actionable checklist for releases and incident response.

Audience: SREs, runtime engineers, kernel/scheduler owners, platform product owners, and oncall rotation.

Quick summary of responsibilities
- API Gateway / Frontend: request validation, auth, and primary throttling. Must never perform model-aware routing decisions beyond policy lookup.
- Dispatcher: multiplexes requests to tenant dispatch queues, enforces SLO-derived admission, applies priority tags.
- Kernel Scheduler: maps ready batches to accelerator kernels, enforces per-kernel credit accounting and preemption points.
- KVCache Service: prefix and response cache; provides soft-consistency contract and warmup API.
- Model Loader: loads models and quantized artifacts; exposes readiness and checksum endpoints.
- Execution Observer: sidecar that attaches traces and exposes metrics for causal attribution.

Table: public runtime endpoints and contract summary

| Component | Public endpoints | SLA / Contract | Fail-open behaviour | Owner |
|-----------|------------------|----------------|---------------------|-------|
| API Gateway | POST /v1/generate, /v1/chat | <= 500ms front-door for small payloads (p50), authentication-required | Return 429 if gateway overloaded, do not route to fallback models | infra-gateway-team |
| Dispatcher | /internal/dispatch/enqueue | Admission decision within 5ms for priority-tagged traffic | If dispatcher unreachable, drop new incoming enqueues with 503 | runtime-dispatch |
| Kernel Scheduler | grpc kernel-run | Kernel start latency bound per-kernel (configurable) | If kernel fails to start within kernel_start_timeout, mark kernel unhealthy and fallback to compatible kernel variant | scheduler-team |
| KVCache | /kvcache/lookup, /kvcache/warmup | Hit latency < 2ms; eventual eviction guarantee | On cache service failure, continue without cache (higher cost) | kvcache-team |
| Model Loader | /model/readiness, /model/checksum | Ready indicator within 30s of load request | If loader failed, route to next compatible model per routing policy | model-onboarding |

Design invariants (non-negotiable)
1) Clear ownership and one-writer for each decision domain. The dispatcher owns admission; the gateway owns auth. No cross-write of priority tags.
2) Deterministic failure modes: components must expose a small set of canonical health states: UP, DEGRADED, STARTING, UNAVAILABLE. Health state transitions must be trace-correlated.
3) Circuit breakers are local and tiered: each component applies local backpressure before propagating upstream signals. Global circuit breakers (operator-configured) exist only for emergency tear-downs.
4) No silent functional fallthrough. On any functional fallback (e.g., model variant swap), the event must be annotated in the trace and increase the fallback counter metric.

Kernel scheduling invariants and policy primitives
- Kernel credit accounts: every tenant receives kernel credits that are replenished on a per-slot schedule. Credits are subtracted when a kernel dispatch begins. The policy must be auditable via the kernel_credits metrics.
- Preemption and safe slice points: kernels must expose preemption checkpoints at token boundaries and checkpoint the KV-store pointers. Preemption requires a handshake: PREEMPT_REQ -> PREEMPT_ACK -> SLICE_COMPLETE.
- Hedging windows: for latency-sensitive traffic we allow speculative hedging to a cold-compatible kernel only if the primary dispatch exceeds hedging_threshold_ms (default 60ms). Hedged requests are recorded with hedged=true tag.
- Admission shaping: dispatcher computes an SLO delta per request type (normal/interactive/burst) and emits admission hints to the scheduler via a compact Admission Hint proto. Admission hints are soft; the scheduler is authoritative.

Profiling hooks and observability contract
- Minimal trace span set per request: front_door -> dispatch.enqueued -> dispatch.dequeued -> kernel.schedule -> kernel.exec -> model.kvlookup -> response.serialize -> response.flush. Each span must include the following attributes: request_id, tenant_id, model_id, sequence_length, token_count, kernel_variant, kernel_gpu_id.
- Sampling strategy: default p0=1% for full traces, dynamic increase to 10% during degraded signals, and targeted 100% sampling for requests with fallback_count>0.
- Kernel-level counters required: kernel_dispatch_count, kernel_dispatch_latency_ms_p50/p95/p99, kernel_preempt_count, kernel_oom_events, kernel_retry_count.
- Continuous profiling hook: every worker exposes a /debug/profile endpoint returning a compact profile envelope (CPU, GPU kernel stats, active batches snapshot) compatible with the runtime lab tooling.

Benchmarking guidance (how to validate surface changes)
1) Local microbench: use bench-runner --profile-kernel to execute synthetic short and long sequence profiles. Use provided corpus under /test-corpus/runtime/fidelity/* for realistic token distribution.
2) Shadow benchmarks: mirror 10% of production traffic (low-risk tenants) to the canary kernel build. Compare p50/p95/p99 and fallback rates.
3) SLO regression check: any kernel change must not increase p95 by >5% at target throughput or increase fallback-rate by >1pp.
4) Cost envelope: report per-token cost delta using cost-estimator v2 with the same traffic shape.

Release checklist for scheduler/kernel changes
1) Update scheduler unit tests and deterministic replay fixtures.
2) Run local microbench and post artifacts.
3) Run shadow benchmark for at least 24 hours against production-shaped traffic.
4) Verify observability hooks present and sampled traces are linked to request IDs.
5) Bump canary to 1% then 10% then 50% controlled rollout with health gates: kernel_dispatch_latency_p95, kernel_oom_events, fallback_rate.
6) Document new config knobs with default values and risks in the change description.

Known issues and mitigations (operationally actionable)
- Issue: oscillating preemption chatter when many small interactive requests interleave with large batches.
  Mitigation: enable preemption_holdoff_ms (default 10ms) that blocks new preemptions for a short cooling window after a preemption event. If oscillation persists, increase preemption_suppression_factor and throttle interactive admission.

- Issue: KVCache warmup races causing model-ready to report false readiness when weights are present but KV warmup incomplete.
  Mitigation: model-loader must expose two booleans: weights_ready and warmup_complete. The routing policy uses warmup_complete when serving low-latency tiers; for best-effort tiers, weights_ready suffices.

- Issue: speculative hedging spikes extra GPU tail usage during sudden p99 latency events.
  Mitigation: cap concurrent_hedge_runs_per_gpu to a conservative value (default 4) and enable hedging_adaptive_backoff that reduces hedging when GPU_utilization>85%.

Runbooks (short, playbook style)
1) Slow p95 kernel schedule (oncall guide)
- Trigger: kernel_schedule_latency_p95 > target for > 10m AND fallback_rate increased.
- Steps: a) Check kernel health dashboard (top kernels by latency). b) Inspect recent traces for heavy long sequence batches; look for 'kernel_variant' mismatch. c) If a new kernel variant was deployed <1h, roll canary back. d) If memory pressure visible, execute per-node eviction: curl -X POST http://scheduler/api/v1/evict?node=<node-id>&reason=mem_pressure. e) Escalate to scheduler-team with trace bundle and node dump.

2) Model load failures during deployment
- Trigger: model.readiness=false following a load operation.
- Steps: a) Query /model/logs?attempt=last and /model/checksum. b) If checksum mismatch, re-copy artifacts from artifact-store and retry load. c) If loader crashes repeatedly, mark model as quarantined and route traffic to fallback model as per policy. d) Notify models-onboarding and create JIRA with logs and loader core.

Telemetry and metric thresholds (first-class signals)
- kernel_dispatch_latency_p95: configurable target per SKU (default 120ms for small sequences). Alert if > target * 1.25 for 5m.
- kernel_oom_events: alert on >1 event per 10m per node.
- fallback_rate: alert if >1% across fleet for >15m.
- kvcache_hit_rate: warning if < 70% for more than 30m for interactive tenants.

Ownership and escalation matrix
- Dispatcher incidents: runtime-dispatch (primary), eng-sre (pager).
- Kernel/accelerator incidents: scheduler-team (primary), hw-partner-ops (if host-level).
- KVCache incidents: kvcache-team (primary), runtime-dispatch (dependent impacts).

Appendix A: Example Admission Hint proto (compact YAML)

admission_hint: |
  tenant_id: tenant-42
  request_type: interactive
  budget_tokens: 256
  slo_ms: 200
  priority: gold
  reason: "chat completion - interactive"

Appendix B: Sample diagnostic curl commands

- Fetch recent slow traces (replace {{request_id}}):
  curl -sS "https://obs.internal/api/traces?request_id={{request_id}}" | jq .

- Trigger local kernel profile snapshot on node-13:
  ssh node-13 'curl -sS http://localhost:6060/debug/profile > /tmp/profile-node-13.pb'

- Query kernel credits for tenant:
  curl -sS http://scheduler.internal/api/v1/credits?tenant=tenant-42 | jq .credits

Appendix C: Example config table (defaults)

| knob | default | description |
|------|---------|-------------|
| kernel_start_timeout_ms | 5000 | timeout to start kernel before marking unhealthy |
| hedging_threshold_ms | 60 | ms threshold to spawn hedged run |
| concurrent_hedge_runs_per_gpu | 4 | cap for speculative hedges per GPU |
| preemption_holdoff_ms | 10 | minimum time between preemptions to avoid oscillation |
| kvcache_lookup_timeout_ms | 10 | timeout for KVCache lookups |
